correctness.rationale: An orthogonal factor pair supports a two-case exhaustive bit-length count. In unbalanced lengths, a disjoint-path matching forbids simultaneous ones at a gap set by the smaller factor, losing (3/4)^(B/4). In balanced lengths, uniqueness of all bit-pair sums forces one factor to have O(sqrt(k)) occupied digits, yielding 2^(2k/3+O(sqrt(k)log k)) choices. Uniform dyadic summation proves the displayed exponent. Reconstructed bounds and independent finite census match original Table 3.
